findings.title: Date override path skips busy-time checks
findings.body: `checkIfIsAvailable` now returns `true` as soon as a date override exists for the slot's day and the slot is not completely outside it, before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check. Existing bookings or calendar busy times that fall inside a date override are therefore ignored when filtering fixed/loose hosts. A host with an override 10:00-11:00 and a booking 10:00-10:30 will still be offered at 10:00, allowing a double booking. The override check should only decide whether the slot is within the override; busy-time filtering must still run afterward.

findings.title: Partially overlapping slots are accepted for date overrides
findings.body: The override containment logic only rejects a slot when it ends at/before the override start or starts strictly after the override end. A slot that starts before the override and ends inside it is treated as available, and a slot starting exactly at the override end is also accepted because the final condition uses `isAfter(end)` instead of also rejecting `isSame(end)`. For example, with a fixed host override 10:00-11:00 and an event slot 09:30-10:30 generated from another host, the fixed host check passes even though the fixed host is only available 10:00-11:00. The slot should be available only when `slotStartTime >= overrideStart` and `slotEndTime <= overrideEnd`.

findings.title: Working-hours check rejects valid split availability
findings.body: The working-hours validation uses `find` with a callback that returns true when the slot is outside that particular working-hour range. If a host has two same-day ranges, e.g. 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 10:00 slot is rejected because the second range returns true when `start < workingHour.startTime`. Since this check runs for fixed hosts and personal-event users, split availability becomes largely unavailable. The code should use `some`/`every` to reject only when no same-day range contains the slot.

findings.title: Slot end is never checked against working-hour end
findings.body: `end` is computed from `slotStartTime.hour()` and `slotStartTime.minute()` instead of `slotEndTime`, so `end > workingHour.endTime` can never detect a slot extending past the working hours when the start is inside the range. In a round-robin event with a fixed host whose availability ends before the event slot's end, a 60-minute slot starting at 10:30 passes a working-hour range ending at 11:00. This should use the slot end time for the upper-bound check.

findings.title: Zero-length date override check compares Dayjs objects by identity
findings.body: The condition `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two separate Dayjs object instances and is always false. A date override with identical start and end, which is the representation this code is trying to treat as a fully unavailable day, is not handled; for a slot starting exactly at the override start, the other boundary checks also fail to reject it, so a slot can leak through. Use `.isSame()` or compare timestamps.

findings.title: Date override day filter ignores converted invitee date
findings.body: `activeOverrides` still filters by comparing the organizer's original `override.start` against `startOfInviteeDay`, without applying the timezone offset computed below. This breaks date overrides when the converted time falls on a different invitee day. Example: 09:30-18:00 Asia/Kolkata on Aug 15 is 21:00 Aug 14-04:30 Aug 15 in America/Los_Angeles, but the override is not active for the invitee Aug 14 day; it is instead applied one day later on Aug 15. The filter needs to use the same converted instant as the minute calculation.

findings.title: No test covers round-robin fixed-host date overrides
findings.body: The only added test checks a personal event with a +30 minute timezone difference, where the override stays on the same invitee day. It does not cover the PR's main behavior: a round-robin event with a fixed host date override, a negative timezone offset/day rollover, or a date override combined with an existing busy booking. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` override/working-hours logic is therefore untested for the cases most likely to regress, including skipping busy times or accepting partially overlapping slots.
